collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HUMOR AND ABSURDITY (HUM-01 to HUM-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Slapstick, silly noises, puns, pranks with permission, ridiculous coincidences, a little funny magic and animals being absurd. Nobody is the butt of the joke: everyone keeps their dignity, and the comedy needs no victim.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A sleepy villager naps in a friend's hut by mistake: let the sleeper rest, or wake them gently.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It is the hottest part of the day. (subject) comes back from the fields half asleep, walks into a hut, lies down on the mat and is snoring within moments. It is not (subject.his/her) hut. It is (friend)'s hut, which looks almost exactly the same from outside. A little later (friend) comes home and finds that (friend.he/she) has a guest.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) tiptoes around all afternoon. When (subject) finally wakes, (subject.he/she) looks around slowly: at the unfamiliar water jar, at the different pattern on the mat, at (friend) sitting by the door peeling fruit. "This isn't my hut." "No." "...Was I snoring?" "Yes." (friend) hands (subject.him/her) a piece of fruit. The next day a bright shell appears on (subject)'s own doorpost, so that (subject.he/she) can tell which hut is which.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) taps (subject.him/her) on the shoulder. (subject) opens (subject.his/her) eyes and says warmly, "Oh, hello! What are you doing in my hut?" Then (subject.he/she) looks around, and the realization arrives slowly. (subject) apologizes all the way out of the door, and (friend) laughs all the way. A few days later (friend) catches (friend.him/her)self walking into (subject)'s hut by mistake. Neither of them is entirely sure any more whose hut is whose.
